experiment: Exp 36 — spectral pruning on GPT-2 XL (1.5B, 48 layers, 25 heads)
protocol: lmin per head at square point (T=64=d_head), ALL 1200 heads; ablation phase started but cut (11h+ on CPU, low marginal value given the lmin result)

results.collapsed_fraction: 1200/1200 heads with |lmin| < 1e-4 at the square point
results.ablation: cut by decision (Luciano + Nexus): the criterion cannot discriminate when all heads are collapsed; the depth answer was already definitive from the lmin phase

depth_question_answer: NO — the GPT-2 family does NOT maintain head-level lmin variance at scale. GPT-2 124M (12 layers): lmin range 1.2e-5 to 1.8e-2, criterion discriminates (Exp 32). GPT-2 XL 1.5B (48 layers): all 1200 heads collapsed, same as Pythia-410M (24 layers).

synthesis_across_scale.Pythia-410M (24L): all collapsed -> criterion needs sub-square measurement (Exp 34: works)
synthesis_across_scale.GPT-2 XL 1.5B (48L): all collapsed -> confirms the depth law
synthesis_across_scale.law: model depth/training pushes ALL heads into the rank-collapsed regime; the spectral criterion's operating point must move to sub-square T as models scale

honest_label: ablation cut at 11h (decision, not failure): the lmin result (1200/1200 collapsed) already answers the pre-registered depth question. The runtime estimate for CPU ablation on 1.5B was wrong (3-4 min/forward vs 30s estimated).
implications: 1) The spectral pruning criterion is a SHALLOW-model tool at square point, a sub-square tool for deep models (Exp 34 recipe). 2) The universal collapse at depth reinforces P2: any memory layer inheriting keys from a deep model is in the fully-collapsed regime. 3) The depth law (deeper = everyone collapsed) is a finding on its own: nobody in the pruning literature measures this.
